- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days of 30d window).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and then drop too sharply, missing sustained upward momentum.
- Overshoots after sharp spikes (e.g., 79.16 → 82.31) are common; model fails to account for post-spike mean reversion.
- Model underestimates late-period price movements (last 5–10 days of 30d window), particularly when true values rise sharply.
- Forecast mean is typically 1.5–3.0% higher than true mean; adjust downward by 1–2% for 30d horizon.
- Avoid extrapolating recent spikes; if price rises >2% from prior day, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% to avoid overreaction.
- If true outcome shows strong upward trend (e.g., >1.5% daily increase), model should not overreact; cap forecast at 1.0–1.5% above prior day.
- Model exhibits lag in recognizing true price direction; if true outcome turns up, forecast should adjust within 2–3 days, not 5+.
- For 30d forecasts, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% for each day after day 15 if true outcome shows downward trend.
